units.text: 1. **Everything through commands.** Every palette, style, swatch, tint, import/export, painting, picking, recolouring and recovery capability of this section MUST be available as a `colour.*` command (table §16.3) and every piece of state shown in the colour palette view MUST be readable through queries. The GUI's colour palette view, editor, tint dialogs, texture properties and export chooser are clients of these commands.

units.text: 2. **No modal paths.** File choices are `path` parameters; the export overwrite prompt becomes `overwrite: bool`; the delete-palette confirmation becomes `confirm: bool` (without it the command returns a structured `needs_confirmation` result with code `colour.needsConfirmation` and a usage summary, and changes nothing); name collisions return `colour.nameExists` instead of re-prompting; live preview in the tint dialogs becomes `dryRun: true`, which returns the before/after values without changing the document.

units.text: 3. **Explicit values.** Creation and editing take complete explicit values (`rgba`, `stops`, `image` + `tile`, per-style `values`) so an agent never needs the colour editor. Omitted optional fields keep their current values. `styleId` defaults to the style selected for the current scene; `"all"` targets every style of the palette.

units.text: 4. **Gestural tools as structured operations.** Paint, paint unpainted, unpaint, dropper, close gap and edit texture are exposed as `colour.paint.apply`, `colour.paintUnpainted.apply`, `colour.paint.remove`, `colour.pick`, `colour.gap.close` and `colour.fillMapping.set`. Each target is addressable either **by object ID** (zone, line, brush stroke or text IDs as returned by `draw.drawing.get`, section 02) or **by point** in one of the coordinate spaces of §16.2. A press–drag–release is expressed as `mapping: {from, to}` (gradient axis), `path: [point]` (paint every object crossed) or `lasso: [point]` (paint unpainted). Tool activation (`tool.*`) is never required for these commands.

units.text: 5. **Zone identity and staleness.** Zone IDs are derived from the drawing's geometry and change when the geometry changes. Paint commands accept the `rev` returned by `draw.drawing.get`; if the drawing has changed since, an object-ID target fails with `colour.staleZoneId` (point targets are always re-resolved). Results return the new revision and the IDs of affected objects.

units.text: 6. **Deterministic results.** Identical drawing content and identical parameters MUST produce identical results. Gap-closing tolerances for commands are evaluated at 100 % zoom unless a `view` is given. Point hit-testing follows §8.1 exactly.
